analysis.title: British American Tobacco (BATS.L): US Nicotine momentum accelerates in October as Velo and Vuse outrun Combustibles
key_insights: Nielsen data through 31 October shows US nicotine industry sales broadly flat over the latest four weeks. Strong pouch growth offset declines in combustibles and legal vapour.

GS estimates BAT gained further US value share. Aggregate sales across cigarettes, modern oral and vapour rose +1.3%, driven by +116% Velo growth after the Velo Max rollout and a +1.9% rise in Vuse sales amid the flavours rollout.
Combustible sales fell -3.4%, extending BAT's underperformance versus the market as key premium brands stayed weak. The US generates c.60% of Group EBIT, so US performance matters most for BAT.
Combustibles (77% of US sales) volumes fell -7.3% against a market decline of -4.8%. Newport fell -10.2% and Camel -9.3%, partly offset by Natural American Spirit at -1.0%.
In branded value, Lucky Strike volumes fell -15.2% while Pall Mall grew +7.1%. The c.3ppt volume underperformance was consistent with H2-to-date trends and modestly better than H1.
Modern Oral (6% of US sales): Velo volumes grew +64.7% against category growth of +10.0%, while ZYN volumes declined -1.2%.

Velo reached 27.4% modern oral share in the latest four weeks, up from 26.3% in September 2026 just before the Velo Max launch. GS estimates Velo Max contributed c.60bps of the sequential gain and is already c.2% of Velo volumes.

ZYN Ultra, launched in June, is slightly over 5% of ZYN volumes. Velo Max reached 44,000 outlets by October and is expected to add a further 55,000 by January, which GS expects to support more share gains.
Vapour (9% of US sales): Vuse volumes rose +0.8% against a tracked legal market decline of -6.8%. Legal vapour is only 30% of the total category.

GS estimates the four-flavour Vuse pod range has captured almost 2% market share and is nearly 4% of Vuse volumes. Flavoured pods reached 25,000 outlets by September and enter a further 25,000 in November.

GS rates BAT Buy with a 12-month price target of 5,600p (25.1% upside from 4,477p). The target blends a DCF (8.5% WACC, 1.0% terminal growth, 5,643p) and a 13.5x P/E on annualised Q5-Q8 EPS (5,557p) at 50% weight each.
GS forecasts EPS (pre-exceptionals) of 355.51p for 2026E, 383.93p for 2027E and 420.85p for 2028E, versus 340.52p in 2025. Revenue is forecast at £26.2bn in 2026E and EBIT at £11.6bn.

market_movers.rationale: GS rates BAT Buy with a 5,600p target. US nicotine share gains from Velo and Vuse are offsetting combustible weakness, and the US is c.60% of Group EBIT. The rating has been in place since 2 Nov 2026.

earnings_insights: GS EPS (basic, pre-exceptionals) estimates: 340.52p reported for FY2025, 355.51p estimate for 2026E, 383.93p estimate for 2027E, 420.85p estimate for 2028E.
GS estimates EPS growth of +4.4% in 2026E, +8.0% in 2027E and +9.6% in 2028E. FY2025 EPS growth was reported at -6.1%.
GS estimates revenue of £26,222.7mn in 2026E (FY2025 reported £25,610.0mn) and EBIT of £11,589.1mn in 2026E (FY2025 reported £11,279.0mn).
GS estimates the 2026E dividend yield at 5.6% and FCF yield at 10.0%. Net debt/EBITDA (ex lease) is estimated to fall from 2.9x in FY2025 to 2.4x in 2026E.
risk_factors: More restrictive regulation on flavours, nicotine levels, marketing, packaging, retail access and product authorisations could pressure volumes, pricing and profitability.
US New Categories growth depends on effective FDA enforcement against unauthorised products and timely product authorisations.
Higher taxes and tighter regulation could accelerate illicit trade, consumer downtrading and legal market volume pressure.
New Categories may underdeliver if adoption, repeat rates or margin progression fall short, and competition could raise promotional and distribution spending.
Faster-than-expected combustible volume declines could outweigh pricing and weaken cash generation.
Litigation, settlement and tax-policy risks could cause material cash outflows.
Emerging-market macro, geopolitical and FX volatility could weigh on local performance and reported earnings.
Weaker trading, higher financing costs, litigation payments or FX headwinds could constrain deleveraging, investment, buybacks and dividend capacity.

tension_points.bull_case: Velo (+116% sales, 27.4% modern oral share) and Vuse (+1.9% sales) growth is lifting BAT's aggregate US sales by +1.3%. Velo Max and Vuse flavours are still expanding distribution, with 55,000 more Velo Max outlets by January and 25,000 more flavoured Vuse outlets in November.
tension_points.bear_case: Combustibles are 77% of US sales and fell -3.4% in sales and -7.3% in volume, ahead of a market decline of -4.8%. Newport (-10.2%) and Camel (-9.3%) remain weak. Regulation, illicit trade and FDA enforcement could limit new-category growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Faster-than-expected combustible volume declines that outweigh pricing, or new categories underdelivering on adoption, repeat rates or margin progression.

theme_stances.key_argument: Velo and Vuse growth is outrunning combustible declines and lifting BAT's aggregate US nicotine sales.
theme_stances.evidence: BAT gains further US nicotine share
